issuer.summary: sUSDS is issued by Sky, formerly MakerDAO, and this axis scores the entity, so it is identical to USDS. Sky is among the longest-running and most audited issuers in the sector — DAO-governed, with a 48-hour governance security module on parameter changes, broad audit coverage and a $10M bug bounty. What holds it below the top of the range is that the contracts are upgradeable and a freeze can be added by governance, which is a censorship surface rather than a solvency one, alongside the structural complexity of the Endgame architecture and a governance-capture tail. sUSDS itself has no independent admin surface — every write path terminates at Sky governance. See the full report.
issuer.summary_source: Internal assessment of the shared entity, held equal to USDS by construction. Allocator composition is reported rather than independently observed. [verified 2026-08-21]
facts: Issuer is Sky, formerly MakerDAO. This axis scores the ENTITY, so it is identical for USDS and sUSDS and moves on both or neither.
✅ Among DeFi's most established and longest-track-record issuers: DAO-governed, broad audit coverage, and a $10M bug bounty.
✅ A 48-hour Governance Security Module timelock gates parameter changes, giving holders a real reaction window on the governance path.
⚠️ Docked for an upgradeable contract plus a governance-addable freeze — a CENSORSHIP surface rather than a solvency one, but a real one.
⚠️ Endgame structural complexity and a governance-capture tail are the other two reasons this is not higher.
⚠️ sUSDS has NO INDEPENDENT ADMIN SURFACE — every write path terminates at Sky governance, so the wrapper adds no separation and inherits the whole surface.
⚠️ Allocator deployments hold off-chain and other-chain assets that are not verifiable on Ethereum, so part of the composition rests on a reported figure rather than an observed one.
